options.label: Retry, then honest failure screen
options.description: Retry the call a couple of times; if it still fails, replace "You're all set" with a screen that says the identity was created but couldn't be saved to this device, plus a Try again button. Never shows a green checkmark over a broken state — matches the "honest, never hype" / "calm under alarm" principles.

options.label: Retry silently, rely on Layer A
options.description: Keep the success screen, add retries, and let the launch-time reconciliation be the real safety net. Least disruptive, but a user who never relaunches still sees an empty wallet after a "success" screen.

options.label: Hard block until it succeeds
options.description: Refuse to advance past handle_registration until the identity is registered. Strictest, but the server-side account already exists, so a persistent Keychain fault traps the user in onboarding with no exit.

questions.question: How should the launch-time reconciliation avoid resurrecting a deliberately-forgotten identity?

options.label: Clear "did" on local removal
options.description: Make remove_identity / forget_identity_locally delete the legacy "did" item, then reconcile unconditionally at launch. Cleanest invariant, but touches the removal path — and "did" is also read by migrate_global_share1_to_per_did, so clearing it drops that legacy share-migration hop for a forgotten primary.

options.label: Only when managed-dids is empty
options.description: Reconcile solely on a wallet with zero managed identities. Heals the stranded-create case (the reported bug) and can't resurrect anything on a wallet the user has curated. Won't heal a failed create on a wallet that already holds other identities.

options.label: Add an explicit tombstone
options.description: Record forgotten DIDs in a separate Keychain list that reconciliation skips. Most precise, most new state to maintain and test.

# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text
changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md
```

- `<id>` is the Linear issue identifier in lowercase (for example, `mm-358`). If a

- `<type>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `fixed`, `removed`, or `security`.
- The file contains one concise, user- or operator-facing Markdown statement. Do not
  include a heading or bullet marker; the release script supplies both.
- Use more than one fragment when a change belongs in more than one category.

Example (`changelog.d/mm-358.added.md`):

```markdown
Release notes now collect user-visible changes from pull requests automatically.
```

The CI gate requires a fragment when a pull request changes a deployable surface:

- server or shared runtime source under `crates/*/src/`, plus PDS runtime assets;
- either mobile app's frontend, native runtime source, static assets, or Tauri config;
- the public marketing site;
- the deployed MCP surfaces — the stdio Custos MCP server (`tools/mcp/src/`) and the

- workspace runtime dependency manifests, the production image/config, or the NixOS

Documentation, tests, design files, CI configuration, scripts, developer tooling, and
other repository-internal changes do not trigger the presence requirement. Any fragment
that is present is still checked for a valid name and non-empty content.

`just set-version X.Y.Z` groups all fragments into a dated Keep a Changelog release
section in `CHANGELOG.md`, then deletes the consumed fragments. This README remains.
== changelog.d/mm-415.added.md
Groundwork for encrypted push notifications: Custos gained the sealing layer that will let a self-hosted instance send notifications through a relay it does not have to trust. Payloads are sealed to a per-device key with HPKE (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-256-GCM, authenticated mode), so a relay operator and Apple both see only opaque bytes and neither can forge a notification your device will accept. Payloads are also padded up to one of three fixed sizes: that does not hide length outright, but it reduces what length can reveal from a per-notification fingerprint to which of three buckets a notification fell into. Nothing is enabled by this change on its own; the relay, the registration flow, and the on-device decryption arrive in the phases that follow.
== changelog.d/mm-456.added.md
A recovery key for identities hosted anywhere. Until now, the wallet's Shamir recovery seed came bundled with Custos escrow, so an identity you imported from bsky.social or any other spec-compliant PDS got a Secure-Enclave root key, monitoring, and backups — but no way back in if you lost the device. The new "Add a recovery key" flow on the identity screen is the same ceremony minus the escrow: the wallet generates the seed, splits it 2-of-3, and publishes a device-key-signed operation that inserts the derived recovery key straight after your device key. Nothing is removed, and no share — nor any part of the recovery key — is ever sent to your PDS; the only thing the wallet asks it is the public question of whether it offers recovery escrow at all. Share 1 goes to your Keychain to sync across your Apple devices; Shares 2 and 3 are both yours to save, and any two of the three restore the identity through the existing recovery ceremony. The flow is offered only where it is the right answer: on a server that advertises recovery escrow, the escrow-backed upgrade is offered instead, and on a server that could not be reached nothing is offered at all rather than guessing. If you later move to a host that does hold shares, the wallet offers escrow once — as an option, not a reminder.

Done. Here's what landed.

## Root cause

`register_created_identity` is the only bridge between the wallet's OAuth-session world and `IdentityStore` (which is what the home screen actually lists), and the call site swallowed every failure before showing "You're all set". Nothing retried it and nothing reconciled at launch, so one failed write stranded the identity permanently — which is why it survived the force close and why the recovery ceremony was your only way out.

I could not pin down which transient caused *your* failure — that needs the device log — but both possible causes (Keychain write failed / the step never ran) collapse to that same single point of failure, and both are now covered.

## The fix

**Backend — [`reconcile_created_identity`](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1478), run at launch next to `reconcile_share1_slots`.** The ceremony persists the DID under the legacy `"did"` account *before* the fragile registration step, so the data to self-heal was always on the device. If that DID isn't in the managed index, it gets re-registered and the global device key adopted. **This repairs your install on the next app open** — no ceremony needed. The DID doc is left alone deliberately: `IdentityListHome` already treats a missing doc as a refresh trigger and refetches from plc.directory.

**Tombstones — [`identity_store.rs`](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/identity_store.rs:18).** The hazard I flagged was real: nothing clears `"did"` on removal, so naive reconciliation would resurrect a locally-forgotten identity. `remove_identity` now records intent in a `forgotten-dids` index **before** touching the managed index and fails closed if it can't — so the unmanaged-and-untombstoned window never opens. `is_forgotten` also fails closed (unreadable ⇒ treat as forgotten), and `add_identity` retracts the tombstone so a re-import isn't blacklisted forever.

**Frontend — [`CreateRegistrationFailedScreen`](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/components/onboarding/CreateRegistrationFailedScreen.svelte).** Three attempts with backoff, then the honest screen you picked.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The **ordering** in `remove_identity` is the whole correctness argument. Tombstone-first is safe in both failure directions: a tombstone written before a removal that then fails is inert (reconciliation only considers *unmanaged* DIDs), whereas a removal that lands before its tombstone leaves exactly the state reconciliation would undo. Additive-first, authoritative-second.
- The two fail-closed defaults point opposite ways on purpose. `load_forgotten_dids` propagates read errors so the writer can't save an empty list over an unreadable one and silently drop every other tombstone; `is_forgotten` swallows the same error as `true`. Withholding a re-registration is recoverable; resurrecting a deliberately-wiped identity isn't.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**One judgment call I made:** the failure screen has a secondary "Continue" alongside "Try again". A pure wall was the option you explicitly didn't pick, and with launch reconciliation as a real backstop, trapping someone in onboarding over device-side bookkeeping is the worse failure. "Continue" skips the success screen entirely and goes straight to sign-in — it never claims success it didn't achieve.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p identity-wallet --lib`: **674 passed, 0 failed** (10 new). The 157 failures you'd see sandboxed are `httpmock` socket-bind denials, unrelated.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`: clean. `pnpm check`: 443 files, 0 errors. `pnpm test`: 171 passed.
- `changelog-check`, `ticket-ref-check`, `docs-check`: pass (fragment added; no new IPC command, so no docs regen needed).
- **Drove the real flow in the browser harness** with the failure injected: create → ceremony → Shamir → handle registration → the failure screen (screenshot above) instead of "You're all set"; a failed "Try again" announced honestly and stayed put; a successful one registered the identity and *then* advanced.

## The bug

Reported from a live run: account creation completed end to end, the app showed **"You're all set"**, and the identity never appeared on the home screen. It stayed missing across a force-quit. The only way to make it visible was to run the share-recovery ceremony — on an identity that had not actually been lost.

## Root cause

`register_created_identity` is the sole bridge between the create flow's OAuth-session world and `IdentityStore`, and `IdentityListHome` lists identities from that store alone. The call site swallowed every failure:

```ts
try {
  await registerCreatedIdentity(form.did, handle);
} catch (e) {
  console.error('Failed to register created identity in IdentityStore:', e);
}
step = 'complete';   // "You're all set", regardless
```

Ruled out as alternatives:

- **Not a display filter.** `IdentityListHome.loadData` pushes a *degraded* card when per-identity loading throws; it never drops a DID. An empty home means `managed-dids` was genuinely empty.
- **Not a partial write.** In `register_created_identity`, `add_identity` is step 1; steps 2–3 can fail without unregistering the DID, and neither calls `remove_identity`.
- **Not iCloud clobber.** `managed-dids` goes through the device-local accessor, not the synchronizable store.

So either the Keychain write failed or the step never ran. The specific transient is not pinned down (that needs the device log), but both collapse to the same defect: **one unretried, error-swallowing write, with no reconciliation anywhere.**

## The fix

**1. Launch-time reconciliation** — `reconcile_created_identity`, run in `setup()` beside the existing `reconcile_share1_slots`. `perform_did_ceremony` persists the DID under the legacy `"did"` account at step 7, *before* the fragile registration step, so the data needed to self-heal was on the device the whole time — nothing read it. An install already in this state repairs itself on the next app open. The DID document is deliberately not rebuilt: `IdentityListHome` already treats a missing doc as a refresh trigger and refetches from plc.directory, which needs neither the handle nor the PDS URL at launch.

**2. Forgotten-DID tombstones** — the hazard that makes (1) safe. Nothing clears the legacy `"did"` account — not `remove_identity`, not `forget_identity_locally`, not migration — so "absent from the managed index" cannot distinguish a stranded create from a deliberate removal, and naive reconciliation would resurrect a wiped identity on the next launch.

The ordering is the correctness argument: `remove_identity` writes the tombstone **before** touching the managed index and fails closed if it cannot, so the unmanaged-and-untombstoned window never opens. A tombstone left by a removal that then fails is inert — a still-managed DID is never a reconciliation candidate, and `add_identity` retracts the tombstone on re-import so a DID is never blacklisted for good.

The two fail-closed defaults point opposite ways on purpose: `load_forgotten_dids` propagates read errors so the writer can't save an empty list over an unreadable one and silently drop every other tombstone, while `is_forgotten` swallows the same error as `true`. Withholding a re-registration is recoverable; resurrecting a deliberately-wiped identity is not.

**3. Honest failure in the create flow** — three attempts with backoff, then a screen that states plainly that the identity exists and is safe but was not added to the wallet list, with **Try again**. **Continue** skips the success screen and goes to sign-in, so the app never reports an outcome it did not achieve. A wall would be worse: the server-side account already exists, and with (1) as a real backstop, trapping someone in onboarding over device-side bookkeeping is the more damaging failure.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p identity-wallet --lib` — **674 passed, 0 failed** (10 new: 5 reconciliation, 5 tombstone semantics).
- `cargo clippy -p identity-wallet --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `pnpm check` — 443 files, 0 errors. `pnpm test` — 171 passed.
- `changelog-check`, `ticket-ref-check`, `docs-check` — pass. No new IPC command, so no docs regeneration needed.
- **Drove the real create flow in the browser harness** (`fresh-install` scenario, failure injected via `__harness.failNext`): create → ceremony → Shamir backup → handle registration lands on the failure screen instead of "You're all set"; a failed **Try again** reports honestly via an `aria-live` status and stays put; a successful one registers the identity and only then advances.

No dependency changes.
